storm.summary_layperson: No thunderstorm threat for this evening's wind window — radar is clear near the cove and storm energy is low, with just a lingering air-quality advisory in the background.
storm.local_effect_blurb: The Sound is running about 10°F cooler than the air, building a moderate marine layer that would blunt any storm trying to move in — but there's nothing on radar to test it against tonight.
storm.detail_html:
Radar (KOKX) is clear near the cove this evening — no storm cells within scanning range, and CAPE sits at just 320 J/kg, well below the threshold for organized thunderstorm development. The NWS Area Forecast Discussion flags a humid air mass and possible scattered storms later in the week, but nothing is inbound for the 17:00–22:00 window tonight.

The only active NWS product is an Air Quality Alert (issued July 31, expiring 11:00 PM tonight) — a haze/ozone advisory, not a severe-weather concern.

The Sound's protective marine layer is present in the background: water is running 73.8°F against an air temperature near 84°F, a 10.4°F difference that the pipeline scores as a moderate marine layer (sound-effect likelihood: moderate). If a cell were to develop and approach from the west or southwest later tonight, this layer would likely weaken or split it before it reached the cove — but with nothing currently forming or approaching, that mechanism has nothing to act on right now.

Bottom line for the window: clear evening, low storm risk, comfortable margin. What would change the call: any cell appearing on KOKX within 50 mi, or instability building above roughly 1500 J/kg as the evening progresses.

wind.tactics_blurb: Sea breeze reinforced by a light onshore gradient — steady, fairly even pressure across the course out of the S/SSW, mature enough to oscillate a few degrees each way. Start mid-line, play the shifts, and expect it to ease from around 7–8 kt down to a light 4–5 kt tail as the thermal fades toward sunset.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
Today classifies as sea breeze reinforced by the background gradient wind (A+). The two-ingredient test is clearly met: the air–water temperature difference (deltaT) is 10.4°F, well above the 5°F gate, and the gradient wind is onshore-southerly at a light 10.1 kt — adding to the thermal rather than fighting it. Sea-breeze confidence is moderate (60% of coastal stations reading southerly, only 29% inland), consistent with a real but not maximally strong thermal.

HRRR's raw forecast direction (176° S) is running about 12° behind what stations are already showing (188° S) — a known model lag in resolving the western-LIS sea-breeze veer. The maturation correction adds 15°, landing near 191° S/SSW for the next few hours; that corrected direction is what's used in the hourly table below rather than the raw model output.

It's currently mid-afternoon, past the point where a sea breeze is considered mature, so expect oscillating shifts — roughly ±10–15° either side of the S/SSW mean — rather than a persistent one-way drift. With the flow running close to due south, pressure should be fairly uniform across the cove, maybe a touch stronger near the mouth and east shore. No strong side bias tonight: play the course center and react to the oscillations rather than committing to one side.

Speed-wise, expect a gradual fade: roughly 7–8 kt at the start of the window, easing to 4–5 kt by 19:00–20:00 as the thermal component collapses toward sunset (8:10 PM). Because this is the reinforced sea-breeze regime and not a pure thermal day, the wind won't die completely at sunset — the background southerly gradient keeps a light 4–5 kt breeze alive through 21:00–22:00 rather than going fully calm. That's sweet-spot one-design range early, drifting toward light-air/drifter conditions by the back half of the window.

No backdoor cold front risk tonight — Boston (KBOS) is reading ESE, not the NE flow that would signal a backdoor pushing down the coast.
